title: When Israel by Divine Command
description: When Israel by Divine Command in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 58, “Supplies in the wilderness”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When Is-rael by di-vine com-mand The path-less des-ert trod; They found, though 'twas a bar-ren land, A sure re-source in God.

lines: When Israel by divine command
The pathless desert trod;
They found, though 'twas a barren land,
A sure resource in God.
A cloudy pillar marked their road,
And screened them from the heat;
From the hard rocks their water flowed,
And Manna was their meat.
Like them we have a rest in view,
Secure from adverse pow'rs;
Like them we pass a desert too,
But Israel's God is ours.
Yes, in this barren wilderness
He is to us the same;
By his appointed means of grace,
As once he was to them.
His word a light before us spreads
By which our path we see;
His love a banner o'er our head,
From harm preserves us free.
Lord, 'tis enough; I ask no more,
These blessings are divine;
I envy not the worldling's store,
If Christ and heav'n are mine.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
